findings.obligation: P3 and E3: a Portfolio created through the API or Lighthouse-Clients without naming the switch starts off. Declared driving port: PortfoliosController.CreatePortfolio. Stimulus must go through that port.
findings.observation: Line 171 reads 'var newPortfolio = new Portfolio();' and line 172 'newPortfolio.SyncWithPortfolioSettings(Read(payload), Mock.Of<IRepository<Team>>());'. The helper rebuilds the controller create sequence in the test, then drives entity and repository directly. A controller regression, such as the route not passing the DTO or constructing the Portfolio with a different default, stays invisible to every changed test. The existing Tests/API/PortfoliosControllerTest.cs shows the controller can be driven, so the port is constructible now, before craft.
findings.remediation: Drive the create stimulus for P3 (no switch, and named true and false) through the declared create port, PortfoliosController.CreatePortfolio or the application-service port under ServicePortHarness. Read the stored value back through the settings GET, keep the real SQLite observation, and delete the re-implemented sequence in Create. Owner: acceptance designer.

findings.obligation: P4 and Y2: an existing Portfolio keeps its stored value after upgrade; a row written before the change reads on.
findings.observation: Line 72 reads 'var existing = await library.ACreateIsSaved(WhatTheCreateSays.SwitchOn);', so the row is written by the new code. The older-client save then reads it back. No row written with the pre-change schema is read, so the historical default path that HistoricalSchemaPatch mirrors is not observed.
findings.remediation: Seed a row through the pre-change schema (the HistoricalSchemaPatch helper), then read it after the change and assert on. Owner: oracle. Non-blocking for craft; completion obligation.
